highlights.title: Two stable kernel updates for Friday
highlights.summary: Linux stable kernels 7.2.5 and 6.18.51 were released, each containing over 550 patches.
highlights.detail: Greg Kroah‑Hartman announced the updates, which address security, performance, and hardware compatibility across the kernel tree. Users are encouraged to upgrade promptly to benefit from the extensive bug‑fixes and improvements.

highlights.title: [$] Accelerating the kernel's build process
highlights.summary: Lorenzo Stoakes used LLM assistance to significantly cut Linux kernel build times.
highlights.detail: By prompting a large language model to analyze and rewrite parts of the kernel’s complex build system, Stoakes identified inefficiencies and streamlined compilation steps. The speedup eases developer iteration cycles, especially on large codebases.

highlights.title: Cognition helps Devin test its own work with GPT‑6 Astra
highlights.summary: GPT‑6 Astra enhances Devin’s self‑testing, allowing engineers to review less code and ship more software.
highlights.detail: Astra is part of OpenAI’s GPT‑6 series and adds cognition capabilities that generate and run tests automatically. By integrating directly into Devin’s workflow it reduces manual verification steps. The model aims to improve developer productivity and software reliability without changing existing pipelines.

highlights.title: Perplexity trusts GPT-6 Astra with end-to-end systems
highlights.summary: Perplexity employs GPT‑6 Astra for communications, code changes, and production monitoring, reducing the frequency of system checks compared to prior models.
highlights.detail: The company leverages Astra end‑to‑end, automating routine messaging and software modifications while continuously observing live services. Fewer manual checks free engineers to focus on higher‑level tasks. This deployment showcases Astra’s versatility beyond pure language generation.

highlights.title: Rapidly scaling online storage to serve over 1 billion ChatGPT users
highlights.summary: OpenAI transformed Habitat into a globally distributed storage platform that now serves 1 billion ChatGPT users at 22 million requests per second.
highlights.detail: Habitat began as a simple Python library for internal data handling. Scaling required redesigning the architecture into a multi‑region, fault‑tolerant service. The upgrade supports the massive traffic generated by ChatGPT’s worldwide user base while maintaining low latency.

items.title: Model: m-a-p/YuE2-3B
items.summary: The m‑a‑p/YuE2‑3B text‑to‑audio model has been downloaded 971 times and received 258 likes on Hugging Face.
items.detail: YuE2‑3B is a 3‑billion‑parameter model that converts written text into spoken audio. Its popularity on the HF hub reflects growing interest in open‑source speech synthesis for applications like audiobooks and accessibility tools.

items.title: Security updates for Friday
items.summary: Multiple Linux distributions released security updates on Friday, covering dozens of packages across AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Oracle, Red Hat, SUSE, and Ubuntu.
items.detail: The updates address recent CVEs and include libraries such as libevent, curl, glibc, and Python runtimes. Administrators should apply them promptly to maintain system integrity across heterogeneous environments.

items.title: EuroPython 2026 videos published
items.summary: All EuroPython 2026 conference videos (July 13‑19, Kraków) are now available online with a recap.
items.detail: The archive includes talks on Python’s future, data science, and community building. Viewers can watch the full sessions or a summarized overview, preserving the event’s content for a global audience.

items.detail: These rare machines, such as the ... (specific models omitted), demonstrated early interest in high‑level scripting on constrained hardware. The article explores how Python was adapted to run within tight memory limits.

items.title: Hackaday Podcast Episode 386: Doomscroll Tamagotchis, Clavichords, and Vibrotrucks
items.summary: Hackaday Podcast episode 386 covers Doomscroll Tamagotchis, Clavichords, and Vibrotrucks, tying into the Retrocomputing Challenge.
items.detail: Hosts Elliot Williams and Kristina Panos discuss quirky retro‑tech projects while promoting the ongoing challenge. The episode blends humor with technical insight, appealing to both hobbyists and seasoned engineers.

items.title: melgarafael/DeskcommCRM
items.summary: DeskcommCRM is an open‑source AI‑powered self‑hosted CRM with native WhatsApp agents, positioned as an alternative to Kommo, Octadesk, and Intercom.
items.detail: The system integrates large‑language‑model agents for sales assistance, supports multi‑tenant deployments, and complies with Brazil’s LGPD data‑privacy law. It targets businesses that rely on chat‑based customer interactions.

items.title: lkimuk/ReArk
items.summary: ReArk is a C++ reverse‑engineering analysis tool supporting HarmonyOS (HAP/APP/ABC) and Android (APK/AAB) binaries.
items.detail: Designed for multiple platforms, ReArk combines static analysis with AI‑driven heuristics to automate identification of code structures and potential vulnerabilities. Its open‑source nature encourages community contributions for additional target formats.

items.title: p1neappleXpress/OpenFlux
items.summary: OpenFlux is a network‑stack research tool that provides a TCP tunnel with pluggable transports.
items.detail: The tool lets researchers experiment with alternative transport modules by swapping them at runtime, facilitating rapid prototyping of new congestion control or encryption schemes. It operates at the TCP layer, exposing a simple API for integration with existing network stacks. Because it is open‑source, contributors can extend the set of supported transports.

items.title: 0xShug0/audio.cpp
items.summary: audio.cpp is a pure C++ inference engine for audio models using ggml, supporting TTS, STT, VAD, voice conversion, and music generation without any Python dependency.
items.detail: audio.cpp leverages ggml’s tensor operations to run inference efficiently on CPU without GPU acceleration. Its highly optimized code paths reduce latency, making it suitable for real‑time applications on embedded devices. The engine’s single‑binary design simplifies deployment in environments where Python runtimes are unavailable.

items.title: Atmosphere-NX/Atmosphere
items.summary: Atmosphère is a work‑in‑progress custom firmware for the Nintendo Switch.
items.detail: Atmosphère replaces the Switch’s stock firmware, unlocking homebrew execution and custom system modules. Development focuses on stability and compatibility, with frequent updates that add new hardware support. The project is open‑source, allowing the community to audit and contribute patches.

items.title: MariaDB/server
items.summary: MariaDB server is a community‑developed fork of MySQL, delivering an open, feature‑rich, stable SQL server with a permissive license.
items.detail: MariaDB maintains compatibility with MySQL while adding extensions such as advanced JSON handling and improved replication. Its licensing model is permissive, avoiding the GPL restrictions of some alternatives. The server is actively maintained by both original MySQL developers and a broad external contributor base.
